answer: The mapmakers at this wharf grind their pigments with shale dust from a single quarry, so every chart they ship carries that deposit's exact mineral fingerprint. A copy painted anywhere else shows store-bought color: vivid, correct, and provably from nowhere. Standing here accrues the same way - each answered epoch grinds a little more of the ledger's own stone into your pigment, grain by grain, and inspectors read the dust before they ever read the picture. Clones arrive vivid and stay hollow; the deposit cannot be bought, only accumulated.
